message.content: This file implements flash swap operations for the RP2040 architecture, providing two functions that write flash data in erase-aligned chunks. The `flash_swap_append` function writes a contiguous range of data starting at an erase-sector boundary, erasing sectors as needed and padding short final pages with erased bytes. The `flash_swap_rewrite` function rewrites an arbitrary program-page-aligned range by copying untouched pages to a spare sector before erasing the destination, enabling block-rewrite semantics without requiring a full erase sector in SRAM. Both functions operate on a `struct flash_swap_ops` interface that abstracts the underlying flash driver, allowing the host to test the algorithm against a NOR model that rejects 0-to-1 bit transitions, unaligned calls, duplicate erases, and overlapping images. The code enforces alignment constraints on offsets and lengths, returns -1 on any failure, and uses a `scratch` buffer to handle partial program pages.
